title: Joint pain or breathing trouble after EVA
disclaimer: Follows general first-aid logic. A flight surgeon approves the protocol flown on a mission.

responsive.prompt: Is the person awake and answering?
responsive.help: Tap the shoulder. Ask loudly: are you OK?

breathing_check.help: Open the airway. Watch the chest for 10 seconds.

breathing.prompt: Is there chest pain, cough or trouble breathing?
breathing.help: Breathing symptoms after EVA are more serious than joint pain alone.

joints.prompt: Is there deep joint pain, skin mottling, numbness or weakness?
joints.help: Ask where it hurts and when it started.

oxygen.prompt: Give 100% oxygen now. Keep them still.
oxygen.help: Fit the mask tightly. Do not let them exercise the sore joint.

vitals.help: Enter what you can. Skip what you cannot measure.

recompress.prompt: Prepare recompression in the suit or airlock.
recompress.help: Only with the Crew Medical Officer. Keep oxygen on during the move.

monitor.prompt: Did they stop responding or stop breathing?
monitor.help: Keep watching. Re-check vital signs every 5 minutes.

cpr.help: Push to the beat. Attach the defibrillator as soon as it arrives.

end.help: The log is compressed and queued on the delayed link.
